candidates.exact_span: Seven representative samples of the sewage sludge that is disposed shall be collected for one monitoring episode at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'one monitoring episode', 'representative', and 'at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed' affects whether monitoring was required for a given period and how missing sample evidence should be classified.

candidates.exact_span: The geometric mean of the density of fecal coliform in the samples collected shall be less than either 2,000,000 Most Probable Number per gram of total solids (dry weight basis) or 2,000,000 Colony Forming Units per gram of total solids (dry weight basis).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Choice between MPN and CFU units, application of the geometric mean across seven samples, and dry-weight basis calculation affect which numeric limit applies and whether reported measurements exceed it.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 2 - Sewage sludge shall be treated in one of the Processes to significantly Reduce Pathogens described in 503 Appendix B.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If this process-based alternative is the operative compliance path, fecal coliform numeric limits and associated sampling may not apply, changing which limits and monitoring obligations are in effect.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 3 - Sewage sludge shall be treated in a process that is equivalent to a PSRP, if individually approved by the Pathogen Equivalency Committee representing the EPA.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether individual EPA Pathogen Equivalency Committee approval exists determines if this alternative is applicable, affecting required monitoring and how unresolved approval evidence is classified.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 4 - Sewage sludge placed on an active surface disposal site is covered with soil or other material at the end of each operating day.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'active surface disposal site', 'covered', and 'each operating day' affects whether this operational requirement—and any associated monitoring or recordkeeping—is applicable.

candidates.exact_span: All sewage sludge that is disposed of in a surface disposal site shall be treated by one of the following alternatives 1 through 11 for Vector Attraction Reduction.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Scope of 'disposed of in a surface disposal site' and selection among alternatives 1–11 determine which vector-attraction requirements and monitoring paths apply to a given facility or period.

candidates.exact_span: The mass of volatile solids in the sewage sludge shall be reduced by a minimum of 38%.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 38% volatile solids reduction threshold is an enforceable numeric limit; interpretation of baseline and final mass measurement methods affects compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: If Alternative 1 cannot be met for an anaerobically digested sludge, demonstration can be made by digesting a portion of the previously digested sludge anaerobically in the laboratory in a bench-scale unit for 40 additional days at a temperature between 30 and 37 degrees Celsius. Volatile solids must be reduced by less than 17% to demonstrate compliance.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether Alternative 1 'cannot be met' triggers this bench-scale path, and whether 'reduced by less than 17%' is the operative compliance criterion, affect which limit applies and what monitoring or demonstration is required.

candidates.exact_span: If Alternative 1 cannot be met for an aerobically digested sludge, demonstration can be made by digesting a portion of the previously digested sludge with a percent solid of two percent or less aerobically in the laboratory in a bench-scale unit for 30 additional days at 20 degrees Celsius. Volatile solids must be reduced by less than 15% to demonstrate compliance.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Applicability conditions ('cannot be met', 'percent solid of two percent or less') and the less-than-15% volatile solids criterion affect which numeric limit and demonstration monitoring apply.

candidates.exact_span: The specific oxygen uptake rate (SOUR) for sewage sludge treated in an aerobic process shall be equal to or less than 1.5 milligrams of oxygen per hour per gram of total solids (dry weight basis) at a temperature of 20 degrees Celsius.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 1.5 mg O2/hr/g TS limit and required measurement at 20°C affect numeric compliance comparison and whether SOUR monitoring was required for aerobic-process sludge.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be treated in an aerobic process for 14 days or longer. During that time, the temperature of the sewage sludge shall be higher than 40 degrees Celsius and the average temperature of the sewage sludge shall be higher than 45 degrees Celsius.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of minimum 14-day duration, instantaneous versus average temperature requirements (>40°C and average >45°C), and what constitutes 'during that time' affect limit applicability and required temperature monitoring.

candidates.exact_span: The pH of sewage sludge shall be raised to 12 or higher by alkali addition and, without the addition of more alkali shall remain at 12 or higher for two hours and then at 11.5 or higher for an additional 22 hours.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sequential pH and duration thresholds (≥12 for 2 hours, then ≥11.5 for 22 hours without further alkali) affect numeric compliance evaluation and whether continuous or periodic pH monitoring was required.

candidates.exact_span: The percent solids of sewage sludge that does not contain unstabilized solids generated in a primary wastewater treatment process shall be equal to or greater than 75% based on the moisture content and total solids prior to mixing with other materials.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 75% solids threshold, calculation 'prior to mixing with other materials', and the qualifying condition on unstabilized primary solids affect limit comparison, monitoring applicability, and classification when evidence is incomplete.

candidates.exact_span: Unstabilized solids are defined as organic materials in sewage sludge that have not been treated in either an aerobic or an anaerobic treatment process at the time the sewage sludge is disposed.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether sludge contains 'unstabilized solids generated in a primary wastewater treatment process' determines if Alternative 7 applies, affecting monitoring obligations and how missing or ambiguous treatment-history evidence is resolved.
